title: Walter Johnson, "Stick and Brush"
summary: Dance praises drummer Walter Johnson, nicknamed "Stick and Brush." Thomas never heard that name but says he could play anything.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: ... somebody that I think never gotten enough credit
was Walter Johnson. Why did they call him Old Stick and Brush?
Why did some people call him Stick and Brush sometimes?

Never in my life. You know Henderson, of all the drummers, I think he's a, you know a leader, a guy that writes music interpreted, Walter could play anything, he wants his tunes to be ... (could not get enough to make any shows, he could play dances, 'Stick and Brush'; well, he'd go from one to the other. I think that's what the writer meant. I never heard that expression before.
Somebody was talking about Walter Johnson and they said, Oh, you mean Old Stick and Brush.
He's a great drummer. Tremendous drummer. We had a situation in '34. Oh, Stan, let me tell you about this.
